raw_signal_observation: The export-options surface exposes a persistent enableOverwriteOutput switch. When enabled, the same surface states that existing files will be overwritten without warning, and the user can also disable showing the export-options page before future exports.
material_claim: The source proves an explicit overwrite mode and warning surface, but not that a collision-level modal, rename flow, or safer default is required. Selecting the guard strength is a product-policy tradeoff involving destructive risk and repeated-export friction, so stronger protection requires OWNER intent rather than repository symmetry alone.
neta_next_move: Ask the owner to state the intended overwrite contract for main export: whether explicit overwrite selection plus warning is sufficient, whether overwrite should default off, or whether file collisions require replace/rename/cancel interaction.
reversal_condition: If owner policy requires collision-specific blocking or confirmation, permit that narrow change. If opt-in overwrite with an explicit warning is deliberate for the main export flow, preserve the current interaction model.
baseline_decision: BUILD: default overwrite off and/or add a per-file replace/rename/cancel confirmation before overwriting an existing output file.

evidence: Owner-authored Issue #2054 explicitly states that the main export function overwrites files only when the user selected the overwrite option, with a warning, and separately identifies other operations where overwrite protection is still missing.
Issue #2667 proposes a different warning/confirmation interaction when overwrite is disabled, showing that the exact collision UX remains a product-policy question rather than a repository fact.
The owner evidence distinguishes the main-export contract from other overwrite paths instead of prescribing one universal guard.
adjudication.decision_delta: SURVIVED: the baseline would strengthen the main-export guard immediately; owner evidence shows that opt-in overwrite plus warning is explicitly known policy and that remaining overwrite-safety work is scoped to other flows, so Neta correctly withheld a generic build.
adjudication.lesson: Destructive semantics do not by themselves select the guard. When the owner deliberately chooses opt-in overwrite plus warning for one flow, generic safety consistency cannot authorize stronger modal friction.
